```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --run --select-best

```

No intervention required — system operating nominally. 🟢

**Takeaway:** The candidate looks *lockbox-robust on average and on minimum*, but it introduces *worse tail drawdown (worst_mdd)* and *very weak tuning min*, so it’s not a clean replacement for the current champion unless your selection policy prioritizes lockbox_min/mean over tail risk.

### What to do next (run these in order)

```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --run --select-best
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml --run
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```

1) **aub_autopilot --select-best**: picks the best module-level candidate(s) based on your configured scoring gates (this is where you’ll see whether the system favors lockbox stability or penalizes worst_mdd/tuning_min).

  - a **worst_mdd cap** (hard constraint), or
  - a **tail-risk penalty** in the objective.

If you paste the next run outputs (especially the selected-best summary and any failure reasons), I can help interpret why the selector is choosing what it’s choosing and suggest the smallest config change to align it with your intended risk profile.
